_comment: ORDER-614 rev 2 DRAFT -- canonical conformance vectors for the S2a attestation policy. One JSON object per line. A line whose only key is _comment is not a vector. SCHEMA and semantics: ORDER614_POLICY_DRAFT.md section 5. Each vector is HERMETIC: the context describes a synthetic git world and a synthetic D1, so a vector never has to be regenerated when the real repository changes -- if a vector had to move whenever D1 or HEAD moved, the corpus would reproduce the signature loop this order exists to end. status=PROVISIONAL means the lead has not ratified it yet and it is NOT part of the frozen corpus. DRAFT: not yet bound into bundle_sha256.

description: The reason the artifact exists: one well-formed APPROVED, bundle current, pin fresh, no expected_post_state. Accepted, and reported as the decision in force. Any criterion made over-strict breaks this vector first.
An empty log is VALID, not an error: it means no decision is recorded yet.
A line that is not valid JSON is REPORTED against its line number; the well-formed record after it is still read and is still the decision in force.
A JSON line that is not an object (Codex round 2, Spec 8) is REPORTED, not a traceback. "The tool broke" and "the file is wrong" must not share an outcome.
A line whose ONLY key is _comment is a header, not a record: it is skipped without being held to R4. The real log line 1 is exactly this shape.

The exemption is the SOLE-KEY form, not "mentions _comment". An object carrying _comment plus any other key is a record and is held to R4. This is the half that stops a malformed record hiding behind a comment field.
A required field present but blank is missing. No row is eligible, so no decision is in force.
decision must be one of the closed vocabulary APPROVED|REFUSED. An invented value is not a decision this policy can interpret.
current_owner must be a current_owner that exists in D1. A decision for a file no proposal names decides nothing.
EMBEDDED:Parent IS a current_owner in D1, so R6 passes -- and R7 still refuses it, because an embedded fact owns no file and follows its parent. This vector is why R7 exists separately from R6.

Record-intrinsic criteria apply to EVERY row, including superseded ones: they were true when written or the row should not exist. The malformed superseded row is reported and the current row is still in force.

REFUSED with an empty reason. MEASURED against the current implementation: `reason` is in the required-field set, so R4 fires first and R8 is never reached. R8 has NO vector that only it can explain -- see the policy OPEN QUESTIONS.
note: R8 is unreachable as implemented (guard shape 3). Ratify one of the two resolutions in the policy before this vector is promoted to CANONICAL.

description: The record in force names a bundle that is not the current one: D1, D2, the reconciliation, the policy or the vectors changed after it was written, so it no longer describes what is on disk. F1 stops the loop, so the owner is reported as UNVERIFIED rather than APPROVED.
Append-only, last eligible line per current_owner wins: a later APPROVED supersedes an earlier REFUSED without either line being edited.

A malformed trailing row must NOT displace the decision in force (/scrutinize, ORDER-613). If eligibility and in-force were computed from different lists, line 2 would be "in force", line 1 would be demoted to history and its wrong bundle would go unreported.

When the row in force fails a stopping criterion, the SUPERSEDED row must not be printed as the current decision (Codex round 2, Spec 9). The honest report is "the record in force did not verify", naming line 2 -- not line 1, which is not in force.

A superseded row bound to an OLD bundle does not block the current one. This is what lets the artifact survive its own evolution: append-only means history can never be re-bound, so demanding it match today bytes makes the log permanently unrepairable.
ORDER-613 D1: a superseded row with NO stale-pin acknowledgement does not block the current row that has one.
The narrowing must not become a loophole: an acknowledgement on the OLD row does not carry forward. Same two rows as V-G4-002 with the acknowledgement on line 1 instead of line 2.
expected_post_state is in-force scoped too: a superseded row naming a post-state that never arrived does not block the current row.
The pin is STALE (HEAD moved away from the blob D1 pins) and the record in force offers no acknowledgement.
audit 8 MAJOR 5: the STRING "false" -- which reads as a REFUSAL to acknowledge -- used to grant the exemption under generic truthiness. Boolean identity, not truthiness.
true is necessary but not sufficient: a structured acknowledgement object must be present, because the flag alone is a blanket exemption that recomputes to nothing.
CONTROL: a fully correct structured acknowledgement is ACCEPTED. Without this vector F2 could be satisfied by a rule that refuses everything.
The acknowledgement names a path other than the one the pin is stale on. Acknowledging a different file is not acknowledging this one.
The acknowledgement names a pinned_blob that is not what D1 actually pins. The value is RECOMPUTED from D1, not believed.
The acknowledgement names a current_blob that is not what HEAD has. Recomputed from HEAD, not believed.
When the pinned path is ABSENT at HEAD, the only correct current_blob is the literal string MISSING. This is the branch that would silently pass if the absent case were coerced to a blob id.

A pin whose path no longer exists at HEAD produces a MISSING note, and a MISSING note demands acknowledgement exactly as a STALE one does. Without the derivation there would be no note and this vector would go green.
A pin whose HEAD blob differs from the pinned blob produces a STALE note. Same input shape as V-POS-001 with ONE axis moved: HEAD:OWNER.md.
SPECIFICITY: a pin equal to HEAD produces NO note, and a stale pin on a DIFFERENT owner does not block this one. OTHER.md is stale here; OWNER.md is fresh and needs no acknowledgement.

Notes apply by path IDENTITY, never by containment. A stale pin on docs/OWNER.md.bak -- a path that CONTAINS the owner name -- must not demand an acknowledgement from OWNER.md. This is the substring-for-identity weakness that produced ORDER-602 H4.
expected_post_state as a bare string is refused: it names no {path, blob} pair and therefore makes no checkable claim.
expected_post_state as an object missing `blob` is refused for the same reason.

Codex round 2, S3: a record may only make a claim about the state of the file it decides for. Binding an unrelated file lets the approved target sit in a state nobody approved while this criterion stays green.
Codex round 2, Spec 3: the literal "MISSING" is accepted by git as an argument and is not a statement about the CONTENT this decision approved.

A short/abbreviated oid is not a blob id for this purpose: the claim is compared for equality against a full 40-hex oid, so an abbreviation could never match and would read as a defect rather than as a refusal.
The oid vocabulary is lowercase hex. An uppercase 40-character string is refused rather than silently case-folded, so the corpus pins the case rule instead of leaving it to an implementation detail.
A record cannot approve the post-state of a file that is not at HEAD. The acknowledgement is correct here (current_blob MISSING), so F2..F5 are silent and only F9 can explain the red.

Codex round 2 probe, found by testing rather than by the audit: a DIRECTORY resolves to a TREE oid that git returns happily. A directory has no content this decision could have approved. The owner here IS the directory path, so F7 is silent and only F10 can explain it.
ORDER-613 D2: the record describes a change that did not happen, or a different one did. Either way this is not the state that was approved.
CONTROL: an expected_post_state that matches HEAD is ACCEPTED. Without it F11 could be satisfied by a rule that refuses every expected_post_state.
CONTROL: appending after the committed bytes is allowed. This is the whole point of the log and must stay green.
audit 8 BLOCKER 3: EDITING an earlier record used to stay green because "append-only" was prose. A byte-prefix comparison is the cheapest real enforcement.
DELETING an earlier record is refused by the same prefix rule.

Codex round 2, Standards 1 (P0): the INDEX is what a commit contains. A deletion present ONLY in the staged bytes, with the working copy intact, must be RED. An implementation that reads the working tree returns green here -- this vector is the one that separates the two readings.

The other direction of the same discrimination, so the rule cannot be satisfied by "always red when staged and worktree differ": the STAGED bytes are a legal append while the working tree is truncated. Green, because the working tree is not what a commit contains.

A log not yet committed at HEAD has no history to protect, so append-only is silent. Reading both sides from git created a bootstrap deadlock: the suite failed because the log was not committed, and it could not be committed because the suite failed.

TRACKED but unreadable from the index is a TOOL FAILURE, reported by name. Append-only cannot be judged against bytes that are not the ones being committed, and "I could not read it" must never share an outcome with "there is nothing to enforce".
UNTRACKED and unreadable from the index falls back to the working tree -- there is nothing staged to judge then -- and the prefix rule still applies to those bytes.

Line-ending normalization applies to BOTH sides of the prefix comparison. A CRLF working checkout of an LF-committed log is an append, not a rewrite. Without normalization every CRLF checkout in this repo would read as history rewriting.

The digest ALGORITHM, pinned hermetically: sha256 over, for each bundle member in declared order, the path bytes, a NUL, and the sha256 digest of its LF-normalized content. The record names exactly this value and is accepted, so F1 is the criterion that reads it.

MEMBER ORDER is load-bearing. The same two files in the other order digest differently, so a record naming the declared-order digest is REFUSED. An order-insensitive digest would let the member list be reshuffled without the record noticing.
CRLF normalization inside the digest: the same content checked out with CRLF digests identically to LF. Without it every Windows checkout would void every record.

D1 absent is a PRECONDITION failure, not a verdict about records: there is no proposal to attest to. Exit 2, distinct from both 0 and 1, so "no proposal" can never be read as "the log is valid" or as "a record is wrong".

ORDER-731 option A: expected_post_state carrying BOTH forms at once is refused. A record that offers two answers to "what was approved" has not made one claim, it has made none -- and without this vector an implementation that accepts both and silently prefers one would conform.

ORDER-731 option A: HALF the SECTION form -- `section` with no `section_sha256` -- is refused. Catches an implementation that treats the presence of `section` as sufficient and then has nothing to compare against.

F8's defect one level down: the literal "MISSING" (and equally a 63-character hex string) is a value sha256 would accept as an argument and is not a statement about content. The SECTION form demands 64-character lowercase hex, exactly as F8 demands 40 for an oid.

FAIL CLOSED, and this is the case the owner is being asked to trust: the anchor heading is not present at HEAD (here it has been reworded), so the approved region cannot be located. "I could not find the section" must never share an outcome with "the section is unchanged" -- that is the one way a narrowed pin could be weaker than the whole-file pin it replaces.

description: MUST FIRE. The row ORDER-731 option 2 creates: current_owner=OWNER.md, owner_ref.path=REF.md, and REF.md has DRIFTED from its pin. The record in force for OWNER.md offers no acknowledgement and must be REFUSED. Before the fix the note was derived and printed for REF.md while the lookup asked for OWNER.md, so F2-F5 were permanently unreachable for exactly this row -- a guard that reports and cannot refuse. Match a record to a note by current_owner identity again and this goes green, which is the whole point of it.

Next branch of the same chain: the acknowledgement names OWNER.md -- the record's own current_owner, which is the intuitive answer and the wrong one. The note is on REF.md, so F3 refuses. This is what forces a real acknowledgement to name the file whose bytes actually moved.
isolation: unique -- the ack must name the PINNED path, not the owner

description: Third branch: the acknowledgement names REF.md correctly but states a pinned_blob D1 does not pin for REF.md. F4 recomputes it from D1 rather than believing it.
isolation: unique -- pinned_blob is recomputed for the PINNED path

description: Fourth branch, and the sharpest one: the acknowledgement states OWNER.md's blob as REF.md's current_blob -- i.e. it acknowledges the OLD file. F5 recomputes HEAD's blob for the PINNED path and refuses. End of the F2->F3->F4->F5 chain, all four now reachable for a split row.
isolation: unique -- current_blob is recomputed for the PINNED path at HEAD

description: MUST BE SILENT, and this is today's real state for the Coverage row: identical world except REF.md EQUALS its pin, so N3 draws no note at all and the split-owner record needs no acknowledgement -- exit 0. It is the minimal pair for V-F2-005: the ONLY difference between them is REF.md's blob at HEAD, which is what makes "the pin fired because the bytes moved" the only available explanation for V-F2-005 going red. Note that OWNER.md is pinned by NOBODY here, so a rule that noted unpinned files also breaks this vector.

MUST BE SILENT -- the specificity half of the ORDER-731 option 2 mapping, and the one V-N3-002 cannot supply. A note DOES exist in this world (REF.md is stale) and the record in force belongs to a DIFFERENT owner, OTHER.md, whose own pin is fresh. It must not be demanded an acknowledgement for somebody else's bytes. Without this, the blocker could be "fixed" by handing every owner that pins anything the first note in the map, which refuses every commit forever and would still pass V-F2-005 through V-F5-003. N4's rule is untouched: the match is exact path identity, and what changed is only WHICH path is looked up.
isolation: unique -- SPECIFICITY of the record->note mapping
